items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to the promotion
of New York state farm products for holiday celebrations
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2069

SPONSOR: METZGER
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in
relation to the promotion of New York state farm products for holiday
celebrations

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to authorize the Department of Agriculture
and Markets to aid in the promotion of New York grown farm products for
holiday celebrations by providing information about New York growers to
vendors who sell such products and to municipalities where vendors sell
them on sidewalks or lots or streets.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends section 16 of the agriculture and markets law by
adding a new subdivision 2-f which will authorize the Department of
Agriculture and Markets in conjunction with the Empire State Development
Corporation, to aid in the promotion of New York grown farm products for
holiday celebrations by providing information about New York growers to
vendors who sell such products and to municipalities where vendors sell
them on sidewalks or lots or streets. Holiday products may include but
are not limited to Christmas trees, wreaths, pumpkins, flowers, and
other similar products.

Section 2: Effective Date: Immediately

 
EXISTING LAW:

The Department of Agriculture and Markets is currently tasked with
promoting New York shellfish, wines, grapes, and grape products.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York farms produce many products for holiday celebrations and deco-
ration such as Christmas trees, pumpkins, wreaths and flowers as well as
food products such as turkeys or apples and honey that are used for
holidays. These farm products are significant to the State's agriculture
economy. For example the Christmas tree industry consists of 875 farmers
that harvest about 275,000 trees. New York ranks 4th in the country in
the number of tree farms.

While these sectors are a substantial contributor to New York agricul-
ture and the State and regional economies, there is opportunity for
growth in sales especially in large urban and suburban markets. This
bill would have the Department work to connect growers with vendors who
currently sell products from other states, whether in stores or on side-
walks, lots and streets. The result will help our farmers and our
State's residents who Want Iodally grown products whether food or trees
or other products.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018 - Passed Senate; died in Assembly

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

summary: Relates to the promotion, market and sale of New York state farm products for holiday celebrations and decorations.
